## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Triple anonymous: the identities of the decision-making editor, reviewers and authors are all kept hidden (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/peer-review-information/review-process), retrieved 2026-11-23. The About page repeats "triple anonymous" and says the journal wants succinct, constructive reports |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No source read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No source read stating that reports are published |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Blank for a stated figure. The 43 APA-survey reports dated since 2022-01-01 show first verdicts of 31 rejections, 8 revise-and-resubmit, 3 acceptances and 1 conditional acceptance; second verdicts: 6 acceptances and 3 rejections (https://apasurvey.philx.org/surveys/export_csv). These are self-selected reports and not an acceptance rate |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. The reviewer-instructions page links general Cambridge guides and says reviews must be the reviewer's own work (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/peer-review-information/instructions-for-peer-reviewers); no journal-specific recommendation scheme is described |
| **Appeals** | Appeals go to the editor-in-chief and are reviewed by the editor-in-chief and/or an editor who did not handle the manuscript; the final decision rests with the APA editor-in-chief and advisory editors (review-process page above) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Yes, a section "Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Tools" on the journal's own preparing-materials page, written in line with the Cambridge ethics guidelines (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials), retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate. Use is allowed with a declaration; minimal non-generative uses (basic spelling or language checking, single words, minor formatting) need no declaration |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with mandatory disclosure for generative uses; same rubric as the Mind entry) |
| **Summary** | AI tools cannot be listed as authors. Authors must declare and describe AI use to generate text or images (including translation of sources or of their own work) or to analyse data, naming the tool and version, dates of use, how it was used and any third-party material it reproduced; declarations go in acknowledgments or a footnote (text), methods (analysis) or figure captions (images). Reviewers must not put manuscripts or reviews into AI tools, and only minimal non-generative assistance is allowed in reviews (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/peer-review-information/instructions-for-peer-reviewers) |
| **Source URL** | https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials ; publisher level: https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/publishing-ethics/authorship-and-contributorship-journals |

## Format

> Source for every row unless stated: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials, retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | One type: "Article". The journal does not accept book reviews and rarely accepts discussions of articles first published in other journals. OpenAlex types 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23: 199 articles, 1 paratext, 1 erratum |
| **Word limit** | 10,000 words or less including footnotes and references; double-spaced; pages numbered. Crossref page ranges give a median article length of 19 pages (25th to 75th percentile 17.5 to 20) across 193 of 201 records, 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=issn:2053-4477) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The page says "must be no longer than"; no statement on exceptions |
| **Abstract limit** | Up to 150 words; keywords requested during online submission |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the 10,000 words. Author-date ("Harvard") system with a reference list titled "References"; page numbers required when a passage is cited |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed (appendices, extra tables or figures, datasets, videos, sound files), published online beside the article and not typeset or copy-edited |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit stated. Tables and diagrams go in the Word file; complicated images as high-resolution tiff or eps. No charge for colour online; colour in print is charged (fees page) |
| **Style / submission format** | Chicago Manual of Style unless the notes differ; US English copy-editing; footnotes used sparingly and no endnotes; Word files (not PDF), LaTeX accepted, Unicode fonts for symbols; ScholarOne submission system; English only; manuscripts prepared for anonymous review with acknowledgements, competing-interest statement and identifying material on a title page |
| **One-submission rule** | The journal cannot consider more than one paper at a time from any author, as author or co-author, until a final decision on the first |

## Soft Metadata

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

> Evidence layers: OpenAlex works records dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (201 records, 191 with abstract), the journal's editorial policy and its live board page. Retrieved 2026-11-23. Regexes are in AI-Research Notes.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Author countries on the 199 articles (articles with at least one author in the country, OpenAlex): United States 83, United Kingdom 24, Canada 13, Germany 11, Australia 7, Austria 6, Netherlands 4, Sweden 4, Japan 3, China 3 (https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=primary_location.source.id:S4210234344) |
| **Editorial-board geography** | The live board page lists 39 entries (some persons appear in more than one list): editor-in-chief 1 (United States); associate editors 9 (United States 6, Canada 1, Italy 1, United Kingdom 1); governing committee 7 (United States 5, Canada 1, United Kingdom 1 for the Cambridge representative); advisory editors 22 (United States 15, United Kingdom 2, Canada 2, Finland 1, Australia 1, Netherlands 1). 1+9+7+22 = 39 entries (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/about-this-journal/editorial-board) |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | "Buddhis-, Confuci-, Indian/African/Chinese philosophy, Daoism or Vedanta" appears in 2 of 191 abstracts (1.0%) and "decolonial, Indigenous, postcolonial, colonial or imperial" in 2 (1.0%). The editorial policy states a commitment to papers that draw on and appeal to diverse philosophical constituencies and traditions (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/author-instructions) |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | "gender, feminis-, women or sexis-" in 13 of 191 abstracts (6.8%); "race, racial, racism, whiteness or slavery" 8 (4.2%); "queer, trans or LGBT" 2 (1.0%); "disabilit-" 2 (1.0%); OpenAlex primary topic "Feminist Epistemology and Gender Studies" is assigned to 13 of 201 works. The preparing-materials page also encourages authors to check whether significant papers by women philosophers or by philosophers from other under-represented groups were overlooked (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials) |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | No single school dominates by keyword: "virtue-" 19 of 191 abstracts (9.9%), "feminis-" 6 (3.1%), "phenomenolog-" 6 (3.1%), "consequentialis-/utilitarian" 5 (2.6%), "contractualis-/contractarian" 3 (1.6%), "analytic" 1, "continental" 0, "pragmati-" 1. Named figures are sparse: Lewis 5, Kant 3, Aristotle 3, Frege 3, Rawls 2, Hume 1, Hegel 1, Nietzsche 1, Wittgenstein 1, Foucault 0, Heidegger 0, Husserl 0 |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** The journal publishes on any philosophical topic and requires accessibility: papers should be readable by philosophers outside the author's specialization, avoiding unnecessary technical flourishes, gratuitous symbols and reader-unfriendly abbreviations (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/author-instructions).
- **What kind of engagement?** Its editorial policy lists five commitments: papers that start trends, papers from early-career as well as established philosophers, papers drawing on diverse traditions, readable papers, and quick turnaround (same URL). In the 191 abstracts, "I argue, we argue, this paper argues" and similar verbs appear in 109 (57.1%), a sign of argument-led papers.
- **Article type and length**: one type, "Article", up to 10,000 words including footnotes and references, abstract up to 150 words (preparing-materials page, https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials).
- **Scope exclusions**: no book reviews; discussions of articles from other journals are rarely accepted; one paper at a time per author (same page).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Blank. No source states what happens to papers that are too technical or out of scope.

| War, violence, COVID | None in sample | 0 of 191 abstracts for each of "war, violence, terroris-" and "COVID-, pandemic" |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | The journal's publishing-ethics page points to the Cambridge research publishing ethics guidelines and contains no human-participant or consent rule in the text read (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/journal-policies/publishing-ethics). Work is mostly non-empirical by keyword count (2 of 191 abstracts mention survey, questionnaire or interview), which is not itself an ethics rule |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers dominate: 151 of 199 articles (75.9%) dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (OpenAlex authorships). The journal also states it will not consider more than one paper at a time from any author, including as co-author (preparing-materials page) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Affiliation rule: affiliations should be the institutions where the research was conducted, supported or approved (preparing-materials page and https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/journal-policies/publishing-ethics); no independent-scholar rule is stated. APA membership is not required to submit or publish |
| **Data transparency requirement** | The journal encourages, but does not require, transparency about sources and selection, and recommends data availability statements and dedicated repositories where evidence exists (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/journal-policies/research-transparency) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Review is triple anonymous, and manuscripts must be prepared for anonymous review with acknowledgements, competing-interest statements and identifying material on a title page (review-process and preparing-materials pages). A public preprint is allowed by the journal and may reveal the author |
| **AI use** | Generative uses must be declared in a defined place and form (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials), retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Open access and cost** | Fully open access; APC GBP 2610 or USD 3655 unless covered by an agreement, funding route or waiver, with waivers requestable after acceptance (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-american-philosophical-association/information/author-instructions/fees-and-pricing) |

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**signal_quality (0-5)**: overall 3. Per layer: OpenAlex counts (methods, topics, countries, types) 4 (191 of 201 records have abstracts, regexes are word-bounded and listed below); journal-specific policies and guidelines 4 (live Cambridge Core pages, readable without a login); publisher-wide policies 3 (AI and preprint pages read; the green open access policy page was not); experiential layer 2 (APA Journal Survey 58 reports, 43 since 2022, self-reported and anonymous; SciRev has no reviews).

**Method note:** OpenAlex works were fetched with page-based paging (no key, no email, one request per 2 seconds; no HTTP 429 occurred). Counts are computed locally over title plus reconstructed abstract with the regexes below (case-insensitive unless a name is marked case-sensitive); word-boundary matching avoids substring inflation. Crossref lists the same 201 records, 191 with abstracts, and was used for the record count and page ranges. Counts are lower bounds for any topic expressed without the listed words; some patterns are broad (for example "cases", "state", "know"), and the "political" subfield pattern that includes "state" is deliberately not quoted in the entry. The scoring convention is stated in Methodological Preferences.

**Regexes used** (all with word boundaries): empirical `empirical\w*`; experiment `experiments?|experimental|randomi[sz]ed`; survey/interview `surveys?|questionnaires?|interviews?`; qualitative `qualitative`; quantitative `quantitative|statistic\w*|regression`; formal `Bayesian|formal\w*|game[- ]theor\w*|model(l)?ing|probabilis\w+|decision theor\w+|logic\w*`; conceptual `conceptual`; argue `I argue|we argue|this (paper|article|essay) argues?|I (defend|propose|suggest|claim|show|offer)`; history `histor\w+|interpret\w+|exegetic\w*`; review `systematic review|meta-analys\w+`; mixed `mixed[- ]methods?`; autoethnography `autoethnograph\w*`; phenomenology `phenomenolog\w+`; virtue `virtue\w*`; feminist `feminis\w+`; consequentialist `consequential\w*|utilitarian\w*`; contractualist `contractualis\w+|contractarian\w*`; non-Western `Buddhis\w+|Confuci\w+|Indian philosoph\w+|African philosoph\w+|Chinese philosoph\w+|Daoist\w*|Daoism|Vedanta`; named figures case-sensitive (for example `Kant\w*`, `Aristot\w+`, `Lewis`); ethics `moral\w*|ethic\w*|normative|obligation\w*|wrongdoing|welfare`; epistemology `epistem\w+|knowledge|know|belief\w*|justification|testimon\w+`; metaphysics `metaphysic\w*|ontolog\w+|grounding|causation|modality|personal identity`; mind/language `consciousness|perception|mental|intentionality|semantic\w*|meaning|reference|pragmatics`; science `scientific|science|explanation|laws of nature`; logic/math `logic\w*|mathematic\w*|paradox\w*|set theory|truth`; aesthetics `aesthetic\w*|art|beauty`; religion-phil `God|religio\w+|theis\w+|divine|atheis\w+`; gender `gender\w*|feminis\w+|women|sexis\w+`; race `rac(e|ial|ism|ist)|whiteness|slavery`; decolonial `decoloni\w+|indigenous|postcolonial\w*|colonial\w*|imperial\w*`; queer `queer|trans(gender)?|LGBT\w*|sexual orientation|homosexual\w*`; religion `religio\w+|Christian\w*|Islam\w*|Buddhis\w+|theolog\w+|Jewish|Judais\w+`; disability `disabilit\w+|disabled`; AI `artificial intelligence|AI|ChatGPT|machine learning|large language model\w*|LLMs?`; politics `political|politics|populis\w+|democra\w+|injustice|oppress\w+`; climate `climate|environment\w*`; war `war|violence|terroris\w+`; COVID `COVID\w*|pandemic`; abortion etc. `abortion|animals?|suicide|euthanasia`; first person `I|we|my|our` (case-sensitive).

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Length**: papers must be no longer than 10,000 words including footnotes and references (Format; preparing-materials page).
- **Article type**: the journal does not accept book reviews and rarely accepts discussions of articles from other journals (Format).
- **One paper at a time**: no more than one paper from any author, as author or co-author, until a final decision on it (Format; Practical Concerns).
- **Language and file format**: English only; Word files, not PDF (LaTeX accepted) (Format).
- **Anonymity**: triple-anonymous review requires a manuscript prepared for anonymous review, with identifying material on a title page (Peer Review; Practical Concerns).
- **AI use**: generative uses must be declared as described; undisclosed use breaches the journal's own AI section (AI Policy).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact I could read; whether a public preprint prevents anonymity is a risk, not a rule (Preprint Policy).

### Soft Tax

- **Accessibility burden**: the journal wants papers readable outside the author's specialization and discourages technical flourishes (Framing Requirements); highly technical work would need rewriting.
- **Cost**: the APC is GBP 2610 or USD 3655 unless an institutional agreement, funding route or waiver applies; waiver requests are made after acceptance and do not influence the decision (Open Access).
- **Time**: the journal states an average of 22 days to first decision and a 12-week aim, whereas 43 survey reports since 2022 give a mean of 2.2 months and a maximum of 9.0 (Review Cycle Time). The survey is self-selected.
- **Style**: Chicago style with author-date references, US English, no endnotes and sparing footnotes (Format).

### Best Suited For

- Accessible, argument-led papers in any area of philosophy: argument-verb patterns in 109 of 191 abstracts and subfield counts spread across ethics (79), epistemology (37), politics (36), mind and language (29) and metaphysics (27) (Orientation, Framing Requirements).
- Single-author work: 151 of 199 articles (Voice & Style).
- Authors who want open access with funding routes: fully open access with waivers and agreements (Open Access).
- Empirically informed philosophy of moderate share: "empirical" in 13 of 191 abstracts and two of the most cited recent articles are of this kind (Methodological Preferences).

### Not Recommended For

- Papers over 10,000 words, book reviews, or replies to articles in other journals (Hard Blockers).
- Primarily qualitative or quantitative social-science studies: "qualitative" appears in 0 of 191 abstracts and "survey, questionnaire or interview" in 2 (Methodological Preferences). This shows the form is rare here, not that it is rejected.
- Authors who already have another paper under consideration at this journal (Hard Blockers).
- Anyone who needs a stated desk-rejection rate or a verified turnaround: only the journal's own average (22 days) and a self-selected survey exist (Review Cycle Time; Metrics).
